title: Money-Smart Friends Could Save You $500 a Year
paragraphs: Do you have a friend who is good with money? If so, that friend could help you save hundreds of dollars a year, according to a new survey.
The survey was done by Talker Research for TaxSlayer Pro, a company that makes software for tax professionals. In July 2026, it asked 2,000 Americans who pay taxes about money and friendship.

The survey found that people who followed money advice from a smart friend saved about $482 a year on average. That is almost $500. Some people saved even more. About one in seven people said they saved more than $800.

Many people ask these friends for help often. Among people who have a friend who is a "money expert," 31% said they ask that friend for advice all the time. About 35% of people even said that every group of friends needs a person who knows a lot about money.
What kind of advice do people share? The most common topics were how to improve credit scores, how to file taxes and how to invest money.
Some people are the money expert in their group. About one in six said they are the friend that others ask for money advice.

Friends can also help in other ways. Most people, 84%, agreed that it is useful to have friends with different skills. Besides a money expert, many people said they would like to have a friend who is a mechanic, a doctor or a lawyer.
